correctness.rationale: At I0=a,S0=1-a,R0=0, let r=(1-a)/a,u=beta*a. The I2=I1 condition is beta*S1=gamma, hence beta=u(1+r), gamma=u(1-u)r, I1=(1+u²r)/(1+r). Descending transversal derivative of beta*S1 at fixed a is (1-a)(1-2u)<0, so u>1/2; S1>0 implies u<1; all subsequent susceptible updates stay strictly positive iff at the crossing beta*I1=u(1+u²r)<1, equivalent to r<(1-u)/u³. Since max such r tends to 4 as u down to 1/2, a>1/5 is exactly necessary and sufficient. The jump S1-S2=gamma I1=u(1-u)r(1+u²r)/(1+r) increases in r, yielding J<(1-u)²/(1-u+u³)<2/5 by factor (2u-1)(u²-2u+3)>0. Boundary approach supplies unattained sharpness. At a=2/5, u=8/15, r=3/2, rational witness gives J=5992/28125. Off-crossing global peak placement follows S_t monotone and sign(I_{t+1}-I_t)=sign(beta S_t-gamma). Independent rational checks corroborate exact algebra.
